domain: Copies a 0xff-terminated byte string (up to 32 bytes) selected by a small switch(arg0) -- one of four fixed ROM string addresses (arg0==0,1,2 pick three specific strings; every other value, including negatives and >2, falls back to a fourth default string) -- into the caller's destination buffer.
behavior: src = default string (0x080af2b1); switch(arg0) overrides it to 0x080af2a6 (case 0), 0x080af2d0 (case 1), or 0x080af2bc (case 2)
copies bytes from src to dst one at a time until a 0xff byte is copied or 32 bytes have been written, whichever comes first

bounded_search.reason: Three respellings: (1) unsigned char with a plain 'c != 0xff' as a sequential if/else-if switch -- wrong dispatch order and no size match; (2) same but with the default-value assigned before the switch instead of only in a fallthrough -- fixed the switch dispatch to match reference's exact binary-comparison tree, but the terminator check stayed a plain byte immediate compare; (3) changing dst/src/c to signed char with 'c != -1' -- brought the candidate to the EXACT reference size (96/96 bytes) with the switch dispatch and every string-selection byte identical, leaving only the terminator-check instruction sequence different.

remaining: Same size as reference, and the switch dispatch (13 comparison/branch instructions) matches exactly. The residual is entirely in how the 0xff terminator test compiles: reference computes it as 'lsls r4,#24 / lsls r3,#24 / cmp r3,r4' (an unsigned top-byte compare with no sign-normalization afterward), while this signed-char candidate adds an extra 'asrs r3,r3,#24' to sign-extend back down before comparing against a computed -1, and an unsigned-char version instead collapses to a plain 8-bit immediate compare -- neither of the two obvious signedness choices reproduces reference's specific shift-compare-without-normalizing idiom. This reads as a narrow, well-isolated residual (one comparison idiom, repeated twice) rather than a broad structural gap, and is a good candidate for a small bounded permuter search over just that comparison rather than further manual respelling.
notes: The four string addresses (0x080af2a6, 0x080af2d0, 0x080af2bc, 0x080af2b1) are read directly from the retained assembly's literal pool; their contents were not decoded (no message-archive cross-reference attempted in this pass).
